composition: Nominal composition of the steel is Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C (i.e. Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C-(0)Cu), with no Cu addition ("0Cu"). The base is austenite-stabilized Fe-Mn with Al and C as the principal alloying elements: Al and C raise the lattice parameter of the austenitic matrix, whereas Mn reduces it, and this balance controls whether intragranular κ-carbide can form. Comparison with the 3 wt% Cu (3Cu) variant shows that adding Cu further increases the austenitic lattice parameter, which is beneficial for κ-carbide precipitation.
conclusions: The aged 0Cu steel demonstrates that intragranular κ-carbide can precipitate from the Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C austenitic matrix even without Cu addition, because its solution-treated lattice parameter (0.3687 nm) lies above the critical value (~0.3670 nm) and its Al content exceeds the critical 6.52 wt% required by the composition-boundary formula. In the broader study, the 0Cu steel is the Cu-free reference; comparing it with the 3Cu steel shows that Cu addition raises the austenitic lattice parameter (0.3689 nm vs 0.3687 nm), which is beneficial for κ-carbide precipitation and enables the co-precipitation of κ-carbide and Cu-rich phase seen in the 3Cu steel. Clarifying this precipitation behavior is relevant to improving the comprehensive properties of austenitic low-density automotive steels.
mechanisms: The austenitic matrix of the 0Cu steel has a solution-treated lattice parameter a = 0.3687 nm (XRD), which is higher than the critical lattice parameter (~0.3670 nm) of the austenite required for intragranular κ-carbide precipitation in Fe-Mn-Al-C steel; because the matrix parameter exceeds this threshold, κ-carbide is able to precipitate from the 0Cu steel upon aging.

Al and C in Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel increase the austenitic lattice parameter while Mn reduces it, so the matrix parameter acts as an empirical index for κ-carbide precipitation; the 0Cu matrix parameter sits above the critical value and therefore permits intragranular κ-carbide formation.

Applying the empirical composition boundary formula 0.208(wt.%C) + 0.098(wt.%Al) = 1 − 0.0054(wt.%Mn) gives a critical Al content of 6.52 wt% for κ-carbide precipitation in the 0Cu steel; since the actual Al content exceeds 6.52 wt%, the 0Cu steel has sufficient ability to precipitate κ-carbide.

Intragranular κ-carbide in the aged steel forms via a nucleation-and-growth mechanism; the κ-carbide is coherent (semicoherent) with the austenitic matrix, giving a low interfacial energy of ~0.025 J/m² and a cube-on-cube orientation relationship with the matrix.

Adding Cu to Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C steel increases the austenitic lattice parameter, which further favors κ-carbide precipitation; the Cu-free 0Cu steel thus represents the lower-precipitation-potential baseline relative to the 3Cu variant.
microstructure: The matrix is austenite (γ) with an FCC crystal structure; its lattice parameter under solution treatment is a = 0.3687 nm (XRD), slightly below the 0.3689 nm of the 3Cu steel but above the critical lattice parameter of about a ≈ 0.3670 nm. Because the matrix lattice parameter exceeds this critical value, intragranular κ-carbide is able to precipitate upon aging; κ-carbide in this system forms by a nucleation-and-growth mechanism and typically appears as dots or bars. The κ-carbide is coherent (or semicoherent) with the austenitic matrix, with a low κ-carbide/austenite interfacial energy of 0.025 J/m², and has a cube-on-cube orientation relationship with the matrix. No grain size, texture, or defect data are reported for this sample.
processing: The 0Cu steel was processed by two sequential heat-treatment steps: (1) solution treatment at 1000 °C for 1 h, followed by (2) aging treatment at 550 °C for 3 h. No further hot/cold working step, atmosphere, or cooling medium is reported. The solution-treated condition is the reference state used for XRD lattice-parameter determination, while the aging treatment produces the aged state in which intragranular κ-carbide can precipitate from the austenitic matrix.
properties: No direct mechanical, physical, or service-property data are reported for the aged 0Cu steel in this study; the reported characterization is structural. X-ray diffraction (XRD) was performed on the solution-treated 0Cu steel to determine the austenitic lattice parameter (a = 0.3687 nm), which is the parameter used to judge κ-carbide precipitation ability. High-resolution TEM with EDS (HR-TEM, JEOL JEM-2100F) and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) were the microstructural techniques used in the overall study. The paper's introduction notes contextually that κ-carbide precipitation in Fe-Mn-Al-C austenitic matrix steel raises yield strength, and that the base austenitic low-density steel class has relatively low yield strength (about 360–540 MPa), but no such value is measured here for this specific sample.
summary: The aged 0Cu steel is a Cu-free Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C austenitic low-density steel that was first solution treated at 1000 °C for 1 h and then aged at 550 °C for 3 h. In this aged state, intragranular κ-carbide is able to precipitate from the austenitic (γ) matrix. As the Cu-free counterpart within the study, it serves as the baseline against which the effect of 3 wt% Cu addition on κ-carbide precipitation (and κ-carbide/Cu-rich phase co-precipitation) is judged.
